facts.statement: The genus Microraptor was first described by Xu and colleagues in the year 2000.
facts.quote: authority: Xu et al., 2000

facts.statement: Many well-preserved fossils of Microraptor have been found in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: Numerous well-preserved fossil specimens have been recovered from Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Microraptor lived during the Early Cretaceous, specifically the Aptian stage, between 125 and 120 million years ago.
facts.quote: They date from the early Cretaceous Jiufotang Formation (Aptian stage), 125 to 120 million years ago.

facts.statement: Microraptor is a small genus of dromaeosaurid dinosaurs known for having four wings.
facts.quote: Microraptor (Greek, μικρός, mīkros: "small"; Latin, raptor: "one who seizes") is a genus of small, four-winged dromaeosaurid dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Microraptor possessed long pennaceous feathers on its arms, tail, and legs that created aerodynamic surfaces.
facts.quote: Microraptor had long pennaceous feathers that formed aerodynamic surfaces on the arms and tail but also on the legs.

facts.statement: In 2003, paleontologist Xu Xing described a Microraptor specimen as a "four-winged dinosaur" and speculated it could glide using all four limbs.
facts.quote: This led paleontologist Xu Xing in 2003 to describe the first specimen to preserve this feature as a "four-winged dinosaur" and to speculate that it may have glided using all four limbs for lift.

facts.statement: Later research suggests that Microraptor may have been capable of powered flight.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies have suggested that Microraptor was capable of powered flight as well.

facts.statement: One Microraptor specimen shows evidence of active primary sequential moulting, a rare fossil behavior similar to that of modern flying birds.
facts.quote: One specimen in particular shows evidence of active primary sequential moulting similar to that of modern volant (flight-capable) birds, which is one of the few known fossil evidence of such behavior among pennaraptoran dinosaurs.

facts.statement: Microraptor was one of the most abundant non-avian dinosaurs in its ecosystem, with over 300 fossil specimens found across museums.
facts.quote: Microraptor was among the most abundant non-avialan dinosaurs in its ecosystem, and the genus is represented by more fossils than any other dromaeosaurid, with possibly over 300 fossil specimens represented across various museum collections.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Microraptor consists of three distinct species or represents variation within a single species, M. zhaoianus.
facts.quote: Three species have been named (M. zhaoianus, M. gui, and M. hanqingi), though further study has suggested that all of them represent variation in a single species, which is properly called M. zhaoianus.

facts.statement: The initial Microraptor specimen was a chimeric patchwork of different dinosaur species assembled from multiple specimens and smuggled to the USA.
facts.quote: The first specimen to be described was part of a chimeric specimen—a patchwork of different feathered dinosaur species (Microraptor itself, Yanornis and an as-of-yet undescribed third species) assembled from multiple specimens in China and smuggled to the USA for sale.

facts.statement: Storrs L. Olson described the tail of the chimeric specimen as Archaeoraptor liaoningensis to remove the name from the record, but Xu later described the full specimen as Microraptor zhaoianus.
facts.quote: Storrs L. Olson, curator of birds in the National Museum of Natural History of the Smithsonian Institution, published a description of the Microraptor's tail in an obscure journal, giving it the name Archaeoraptor liaoningensis in an attempt to remove the name from the paleornithological record by assigning it to the part least likely to be a bird.

facts.statement: There is debate regarding whether Storrs L. Olson successfully met all formal requirements to establish Archaeoraptor liaoningensis as a valid taxon.
facts.quote: However, there is some doubt whether Olson in fact succeeded in meeting all the formal requirements for establishing a new taxon.

facts.statement: Due to its frequent use and proper description, Microraptor is considered a nomen protectum while Archaeoraptor is a nomen vanum.
facts.quote: In addition, Xu's name for the type specimen (Microraptor) was subsequently used more frequently than the original name; as such, this and the chimeric nature of the specimen would render the name "Archaeoraptor" a nomen vanum (as it was improperly described) and the junior synonym Microraptor a nomen protectum (as it has been used in more published works than "Archaeoraptor" and was properly described).

facts.statement: Mark Norell and colleagues described an unnamed Microraptor specimen, BPM 1 3-13, in 2002.
facts.quote: In 2002 Mark Norell et al. described another specimen, BPM 1 3-13, which they did not name or refer to an existing species.

facts.statement: The genus name Cryptovolans is derived from the Greek word for "hidden" and the Latin word for "flying".
facts.quote: The generic name was derived from Greek kryptos, "hidden", and Latin volans, "flying".

facts.statement: Cryptovolans pauli specimens were collected from the early Albian Jiufotang Formation in Liaoning, China.
facts.quote: The type specimens of C. pauli were collected from the Jiufotang Formation, dating from the early Albian and now belong to the collection of the Paleontology Museum of Beipiao, in Liaoning, China.

facts.statement: Studies indicate that features distinguishing Cryptovolans are not unique and appear in varying degrees across Microraptor specimens.
facts.quote: Subsequent studies (and more specimens of Microraptor) have shown that the features used to distinguish Cryptovolans are not unique, but are present to varying degrees across various specimens.

facts.statement: In 2004, Phil Senter and colleagues suggested that Cryptovolans pauli and Microraptor gui are junior synonyms of Microraptor zhaoianus due to individual variation.
facts.quote: In a review by Phil Senter and colleagues in 2004, the scientists suggested that all these features represented individual variation across various age groups of a single Microraptor species, making the name Cryptovolans pauli and Microraptor gui junior synonyms of Microraptor zhaoianus.

facts.statement: Specimen BMNHC PH881 revealed previously unknown features, including probably glossy-black iridescent plumage.
facts.quote: A new specimen of Microraptor, BMNHC PH881, showed several features previously unknown in the animal, including the probably glossy-black iridescent plumage coloration.

facts.statement: Microraptor is the most abundant non-avian dinosaur fossil type found in the Jiufotang Formation.
facts.quote: In fact, Microraptor is the most abundant non-avialan dinosaur fossil type found in this formation.

facts.statement: In 2002, Norell and colleagues described specimen BPM 1 3-13 as the first dinosaur known to possess flight feathers on both its legs and arms.
facts.quote: Norell et al. (2002) described BPM 1 3-13 as the first dinosaur known to have flight feathers on its legs as well as on its arms.

facts.statement: The first specimens of Microraptor were discovered in 2001, and four additional specimens were acquired by the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology from private collectors between 2001 and 2003.
facts.quote: The first of these specimens was discovered in 2001, and between 2001 and 2003 four more specimens were bought from private collectors by Xu's museum, the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology.

facts.statement: Research by Xu and colleagues in 2003 suggested that early dromaeosaurs were likely small, lived in trees, and were capable of gliding.
facts.quote: The work of Xu et al. (2003) suggested that basal dromaeosaurs were probably small, arboreal, and could glide.

facts.statement: Microraptor was one of the smallest non-avian dinosaurs, with the holotype of M. gui measuring 77 cm in length, having a wingspan of 88 to 94 cm, and weighing between 0.5 and 1.4 kg.
facts.quote: Microraptor was among the smallest-known non-avian dinosaurs, with the holotype of M. gui measuring 77 cm in length, 88 - 94 cm in wingspan and weighing 0.5 - 1.4 kg.

facts.statement: Larger specimens of Microraptor measured at least 80 cm in length, had wingspans exceeding 99 cm, and weighed between 1.25 and 1.88 kg.
facts.quote: There are larger specimens which would have measured at least 80 cm in length, more than 99 cm in wingspan and weighed 1.25 - 1.88 kg.

facts.statement: Microraptor had a thick body covering of feathers and a diamond-shaped fan at the end of its tail, which may have provided stability during flight.
facts.quote: Their bodies had a thick covering of feathers, with a diamond-shaped fan on the end of the tail (possibly for added stability during flight).

facts.statement: In 2003, Xu and colleagues compared the long plumes on Microraptor's head to those found on the Philippine eagle.
facts.quote: Xu et al. (2003) compared the longer plumes on Microraptors head to those of the Philippine eagle.

facts.statement: While some specimens show bands of dark and light that may indicate color patterns, at least some individuals of Microraptor almost certainly possessed an iridescent black coloration.
facts.quote: Bands of dark and light present on some specimens may indicate color patterns present in life, though at least some individuals almost certainly possessed an iridescent black coloration.

facts.statement: In March 2012, Li and colleagues determined the plumage coloration of Microraptor using the new specimen BMNHC PH881, which also revealed several previously unknown features.
facts.quote: In March 2012, Quanguo Li et al. determined the plumage coloration of Microraptor based on the new specimen BMNHC PH881, which also showed several other features previously unknown in Microraptor.

facts.statement: Analysis of melanosomes in Microraptor revealed rod-shaped, narrow cells arranged in stacked layers similar to a modern starling, indicating a black, glossy, and iridescent plumage.
facts.quote: In Microraptor, these cells were shaped in a manner consistent with black, glossy coloration in modern birds. These rod-shaped, narrow melanosomes were arranged in stacked layers, much like those of a modern starling, and indicated iridescence in the plumage of Microraptor.

facts.statement: While the function of Microraptor's iridescence is unknown, it has been suggested that the animal used its glossy coat for communication or sexual display, similar to modern iridescent birds.
facts.quote: Though the researchers state that the true function of the iridescence is yet unknown, it has been suggested that the tiny dromaeosaur was using its glossy coat as a form of communication or sexual display, much as in modern iridescent birds.

facts.statement: Microraptor possessed long pennaceous feathers on its arms and hands measuring 10 to 20 cm and on its legs and feet measuring 11 to 15 cm.
facts.quote: It had long pennaceous feathers on arms and hands 10 – 20 cm with legs and feet 11 – 15 cm.

facts.statement: Microraptor had true flight feathers on its legs with asymmetrical vanes on its arm, leg, and tail feathers similar to modern birds.
facts.quote: The long feathers on the legs of Microraptor were true flight feathers as seen in modern birds, with asymmetrical vanes on the arm, leg, and tail feathers.

facts.statement: Researchers originally hypothesized that Microraptor was an arboreal glider because its hindwings would have hindered ground running.
facts.quote: It was originally thought that Microraptor was a glider, and probably lived mainly in trees, because the hindwings anchored to the feet of Microraptor would have hindered their ability to run on the ground.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists suggest Microraptor used its wings to parachute from trees to ambush prey, though this is debated.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists have suggested that feathered dinosaurs used their wings to parachute from trees, possibly to attack or ambush prey on the ground, as a precursor to gliding or true flight.

facts.statement: A 2007 study by Chatterjee and Templin found Microraptor's wing surface was too narrow for successful parachuting from significant heights.
facts.quote: In their 2007 study, Chatterjee and Templin tested this hypothesis as well, and found that the combined wing surface of Microraptor was too narrow to successfully parachute to the ground without injury from any significant height.

facts.statement: Wind tunnel experiments suggest Microraptor was most efficient when gliding between low elevations by sustaining high lift at the expense of high drag.
facts.quote: Wind tunnel experiments have demonstrated that sustaining a high-lift coefficient at the expense of high drag was likely the most efficient strategy for Microraptor when gliding between low elevations.

facts.statement: Anatomical studies show Microraptor's limb proportions resemble ground birds rather than climbers, challenging the arboreal glider hypothesis.
facts.quote: However, the idea that Microraptor was an arboreal glider relies on it to have regularly climbed or even lived in trees, when study of its anatomy have shown that its limb proportions fall in line with modern ground birds rather than climbers, and its skeleton shows none of the expected adaptations in animals specialized for climbing trees.

facts.statement: Paleontologist Stephen Czerkas argued Microraptor was a powered flier, possibly better than Archaeopteryx, based on its fused sternum and shoulder girdle features.
facts.quote: Describing specimens originally referenced as a distinctive species (Cryptovolans pauli), paleontologist Stephen Czerkas argued Microraptor may have been a powered flier, and indeed possibly a better flyer than Archaeopteryx.

facts.statement: Most scientists agree Microraptor had anatomical features for flight, though likely less advanced than modern birds.
facts.quote: Today, most scientists agree that Microraptor had the anatomical features expected of a flying animal, though it would have been a less advanced form of flight compared to birds.

facts.statement: Some studies suggest Microraptor's shoulder joint was too primitive for a full flapping flight stroke.
facts.quote: For example, some studies suggest the shoulder joint was too primitive to allow a full flapping flight stroke.

facts.statement: Other scientists argue Microraptor's curved shoulder girdle allowed for a nearly vertical wing upstroke, supporting powered flight.
facts.quote: However, other scientists have argued that the shoulder girdle in some paravian theropods, including Microraptor, is curved in such a way that the shoulder joint could only have been positioned high on the back, allowing for a nearly vertical upstroke of the wing.

facts.statement: Studies demonstrate Microraptor's wings were large enough to generate lift for powered launching without a fully vertical flight stroke.
facts.quote: Other studies have demonstrated that the wings of Microraptor were large enough to generate the lift necessary for powered launching into flight even without a fully vertical flight stroke.

facts.statement: A 2016 study demonstrated Microraptor was capable of wing-assisted incline running, leaping, and ground-based launching.
facts.quote: A 2016 study of incipient flight ability in paravians demonstrated that Microraptor was capable of wing-assisted incline running, as well as wing-assisted leaping and even ground-based launching.

facts.statement: Some researchers argue Microraptor's flight capability suggests dromaeosaurids like Deinonychus were secondarily flightless.
facts.quote: Stephen Czerkas, Gregory S. Paul, and others have argued that the fact Microraptor could fly and yet is also very clearly a dromaeosaurid suggests that the Dromaeosauridae, including later and larger species such as Deinonychus, were secondarily flightless.

facts.statement: Xu and colleagues suggested dromaeosaurid ancestors were arboreal gliders, but later discoveries of primitive species with short forelimbs cast doubt on this.
facts.quote: The work of Xu and colleagues also suggested that the ancestors of dromaeosaurids were probably small, arboreal, and capable of gliding, although later discoveries of more primitive dromaeosaurids with short forelimbs unsuitable for gliding have cast doubt on this view.

facts.statement: Studies conclude Microraptor likely evolved flight features independently of bird ancestors.
facts.quote: These studies concluded that Microraptor probably evolved flight and its associated features (fused sternum, alula, etc.) independently of the ancestors of birds.

facts.statement: A 2024 analysis by Kiat and O'Connor found Microraptor had remex morphologies consistent with modern flying birds, unlike secondarily flightless anchiornithids and Caudipteryx.
facts.quote: In 2024, Kiat and O'Connor analyzed that Mesozoic birds and Microraptor had remex morphologies that are consistent with modern volant birds, while anchiornithids and Caudipteryx were secondarily flightless.

facts.statement: In 2005, Sankar Chatterjee suggested Microraptor's forewings and hindwings were on different levels like a biplane, as an overlaid posture would be anatomically impossible.
facts.quote: Sankar Chatterjee suggested in 2005 that, in order for Microraptor to glide or fly, the forewings and hindwings must have been on different levels (as on a biplane) and not overlaid (as on a dragonfly), and that the latter posture would have been anatomically impossible.

facts.statement: Chatterjee determined Microraptor likely used a phugoid gliding style, swooping in a deep U-shaped curve between perches.
facts.quote: Using this biplane model, Chatterjee was able to calculate possible methods of gliding and determined that Microraptor most likely employed a phugoid style of gliding: launching itself from a perch, the animal would have swooped downward in a deep U-shaped curve and then lifted again to land on another tree.

facts.statement: Some paleontologists doubt the biplane hypothesis for Microraptor and have proposed alternative configurations.
facts.quote: Some paleontologists have doubted the biplane hypothesis, and have proposed other configurations.

facts.statement: A 2010 study found Microraptor's biplane model was structurally deficient and required an unlikely heavy-headed weight distribution for stable gliding.
facts.quote: A 2010 study by Alexander et al. described the construction of a lightweight three-dimensional physical model used to perform glide tests. Using several hindleg configurations for the model, they found that the biplane model, while not unreasonable, was structurally deficient and needed a heavy-headed weight distribution for stable gliding, which they deemed unlikely.

facts.statement: Brougham and Brusatte criticized Alexander's model for having hip anatomy inconsistent with other dromaeosaurs.
facts.quote: Brougham and Brusatte criticized the anatomy of the model used by Alexander and his team, noting that the hip anatomy was not consistent with other dromaeosaurs.

facts.statement: Brougham and Brusatte argued Alexander's model used a crushed flat specimen that did not reflect Microraptor's actual anatomy.
facts.quote: Alexander's team used a specimen of Microraptor which was crushed flat to make their model, which Brougham and Brusatte argued did not reflect its actual anatomy.

facts.statement: Microraptor likely had awkward ground movement because its hindwing feathers extended over most of its foot.
facts.quote: Due to the extent of the hindwings onto most of the animal's foot, many scientists have suggested that Microraptor would have been awkward during normal ground movement or running.

facts.statement: Microraptor's front wing feathers hindered ground movement due to limited wrist motion and extreme feather length.
facts.quote: The front wing feathers would also have hindered Microraptor when on the ground, due to the limited range of motion in the wrist and the extreme length of the wing feathers.

facts.statement: A 2010 study by Corwin Sullivan and colleagues found that Microraptor's wing feathers would drag on the ground even when folded as much as possible.
facts.quote: A 2010 study by Corwin Sullivan and colleagues showed that, even with the wing folded as far as possible, the feathers would still have dragged along the ground if the arms were held in a neutral position, or extended forward as in a predatory strike.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Microraptor represents a four-winged stage in the evolution of modern birds or an evolutionary side-branch with no descendants.
facts.quote: The unique wing arrangement found in Microraptor raised the question of whether the evolution of flight in modern birds went through a four-winged stage, or whether four-winged gliders like Microraptor were an evolutionary side-branch that left no descendants.

facts.statement: The mammal in Microraptor's gut had an estimated snout-to-vent length of 80 mm and a mass of 13–43 g.
facts.quote: The foot skeleton is similar to those of Eomaia and Sinodelphys. It corresponds to an animal with an estimated snout to vent length of 80 mm and a mass of 13 – 43 g.

facts.statement: A 2011 study by Jingmai O'Connor and coauthors described a Microraptor gui specimen containing bones of an arboreal enantiornithean bird, including a partial wing and feet.
facts.quote: In the 6 December 2011 issue of Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Jingmai O'Connor and coauthors described a specimen of Microraptor gui containing bones of an arboreal enantiornithean bird in its abdomen, specifically a partial wing and feet.

facts.statement: Researchers argued that a Microraptor gui specimen showed probable adaptation to a fish-eating diet, citing the first three mandibular teeth being inclined anterodorsally.
facts.quote: They further argued that the specimen showed a probable adaptation to a fish-eating diet, pointing to the first three teeth of the mandible being inclined anterodorsally, a characteristic often associated with piscivory.

facts.statement: Hone and colleagues (2022) questioned the reliability of predation interpretations for Microraptor gut contents, suggesting they could equally be attributed to scavenging.
facts.quote: However, Hone and colleagues (2022) questioned the reliability of these interpretations and wrote that both could just as equally be attributed to scavenging.

facts.statement: Microraptor likely passed indigestible fur, feathers, and bone bits in its droppings instead of producing gastric pellets.
facts.quote: This suggests that Microraptor passed indigestible fur, feathers, and bits of bone in its droppings instead of producing pellets.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Microraptor hunted at night; eye morphology suggests nocturnal hunting, but dark and glossy plumage may indicate otherwise.
facts.quote: Based on the morphology of the scleral ring of the eye, it has been suggested Microraptor hunted at night. However, the discovery of dark and glossy plumage in Microraptor may suggest otherwise, as no modern birds with comparable plumage are known to be nocturnal.

facts.statement: Morphometric analysis suggests Microraptor may have had a raptorial lifestyle similar to modern hawks.
facts.quote: Morphometric analysis of the size and shape of its pedal claws, paired with assessment of its joint articulations and pedal soft tissues using laser-stimulated fluorescence, suggests that Microraptor may have had a similar raptorial lifestyle to modern hawks.

facts.quote: En 2010 los investigadores anunciaron que la preparación adicional del espécimen tipo de M. zhaoianus reveló posibles contenidos preservados del estómago. Estos consistían en huesos de mamíferos, incluyendo posibles fragmentos de cráneo, miembros y de vértebras así como un pie entero.

facts.statement: In December 2011, Jingmai O'Connor and colleagues described a Microraptor specimen containing bird bones in its abdomen, specifically a partial wing and a foot.
facts.quote: En la edición del 6 de diciembre de 2011 de Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, Jingmai O'Connor y colaboradores describieron un ejemplar de Microraptor que contenía huesos de ave en su abdomen, más específicamente un ala parcial y el pie.

facts.statement: In 2013, fish were announced to have been found in the abdominal cavity of a Microraptor specimen.
facts.quote: En 2013 se anunció que se habían encontrado peces en la cavidad abdominal de un espécimen de Microraptor.

facts.statement: In 2019, a new genus of armored lizard, Indrasaurus, was described from a specimen found in the stomach of a Microraptor.
facts.quote: En 2019, se describió un nuevo género de lagarto esclerogloso, Indrasaurus a partir de un espécimen encontrado en el estómago de un Microraptor.

facts.statement: Unlike its paravian relatives such as Anchiornis, Microraptor has never been found with gastric granules, despite four specimens preserving stomach contents.
facts.quote: A diferencia de sus compañeros paravianos como Anchiornis , Microraptor nunca se ha encontrado con gránulos gástricos, a pesar de la existencia de cuatro muestras de Microraptor que preservan el contenido del estómago.

facts.statement: Based on the size of the sclerotic rings in the eye, it was concluded that Microraptor hunted at night.
facts.quote: Basándose en el tamaño de los anillos escleróticos del ojo, se concluyó que Microraptor cazaba de noche.

facts.statement: However, the discovery of iridescent plumage in Microraptor has cast doubt on the conclusion that it hunted at night, as no bird with such plumage is known to be nocturnal.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, el descubrimiento del plumaje iridiscente en Microraptor ha hecho dudar de esa conclusión, ya que no se conoce ninguna ave que tenga plumaje que sea nocturna.

facts.statement: The Indrasaurus bones lacked significant bite marks or scars, indicating Microraptor died shortly after eating the lizard and before significant digestion occurred.
facts.quote: Los huesos de Indrasaurus carecían de picaduras y cicatrices marcadas, lo que indica que el Microraptor murió poco después de comer la lagartija y antes de que se produjera una digestión significativa.

facts.statement: This suggests Microraptor passed undigested fur, feathers, and bone fragments in its feces instead of producing gastric granules.
facts.quote: Esto sugiere que Microraptor pasó pelaje, plumas y trozos de hueso no digeribles en sus excrementos en lugar de producir gránulos.

facts.statement: Good preservation of the jaw shows the first three teeth were inclined anterodorsally, a trait frequently associated with fish predation.
facts.quote: La buena preservación de la mandíbula muestra que los primeros tres dientes estaban inclinados anterodorsalmente, un rasgo frecuentemente asociado con la depredación de peces.

facts.statement: A 2026 study by Hefler et al. reported evidence that interactions between the forewings and hindwings of Microraptor had a beneficial impact on flight flow dynamics.
facts.quote: Hefler et al. (2026) study the aerodynamics of Microraptor during flight, reporting evidence of beneficial impact of forewing–hindwing interactions on flow dynamics.
